correctness.rationale: Both divisor sums are multiplicative, and exact prime-power ratios rho_p(a) are correct. For each exponent cylinder supported on primes <=31 with R>=1, the squarefree >31 tail multiplies R by factors (1+1/q)>1; finitely many all-smooth equality exceptions do not affect density. CRT/squarefree sieve gives density sum W/D*prod_{q>31}(1-1/q^2). Independently compiled a new boost::multiprecision cpp_int enumerator with different accumulation structure, exhaustively enumerating 7,676,370 configurations: W=28604085934433764658299339805699268088627200, 2,837,267 accepted, six equal, and D=36886693308870756519590386924324100736000000. Independent Fraction algebra reproduced the exact pi^-2 coefficient and the strict rational 77% inequality via pi<22/7. Finite arithmetic is exhaustive for the explicitly defined cylinder, but not a census of all integers.
residual_risks: The true density is undetermined. Stronger recent or unindexed certificates may exist; Resultary and public searches are not exhaustive priority proof.
Finite enumerator certifies only the explicit 11-prime cylinder; positivity outside it is neither proven nor required.

originality.rationale: The 2013 Trudgian question, 6/pi^2 squarefree bound and 0.778307 empirical fraction are distinct from the rigorous 77% bound. The explicit previously published 0.753659... cylinder has only six primes and exponent caps five, whereas this certificate chooses eleven primes with varying caps and recomputes all rational weights. The Erdos–Wintner theorem guarantees density existence and generic Euler products count exponent restrictions, but neither determines which 7,676,370 local patterns pass the weighted product condition. No inspected source supplies a dominating certified 0.77 lower bound. OEIS A322446 lists finite sample counts, not an asymptotic inequality. The inspected Resultary RESULT.md has W over 46,656 vectors and constant 0.753659844, different from this exact 7,676,370-vector certificate. The earlier lower bound is strictly weaker numerically and uses a narrower cylinder; the new bound does not follow merely by quoting the old fraction. It reuses the same standard method with a stronger exact finite certificate; it neither proves delta=0.778307 nor any upper bound.
